focus: Post-re-pin regeneration coverage: dsh links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, trigger index, advisor graph
noveltyJustification: All 8 findings were new to this lineage; the generator check contracts had not been read before iteration 3 and one directly corrects the dispatch brief.
answeredQuestions: Q3: Which runtime surfaces must be re-pinned or regenerated after a re-pin (dsh skill links, runtime mirrors, hook registrations, trigger index, advisor graph), and how should the engine express them?

keyFindings.text: Barter's manifest already declares a `hook-registrations` pair — a regenerate step and its `--check` verify — pointing at `sync-hook-registrations.cjs`, so the brief's list is wrong on that item: hook registration regeneration is expressible and already expressed. [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1394] [SOURCE: /Users/michelkerkmeester/MEGA/Development/Skilled/barter/ai-speckit/skilled/barter-overlays/overlay-manifest.json:1502]

The dsh skill sync is a clean regenerate/verify pair the engine can express today — `sync-skills-dsh.cjs` writes without flags and `--check` reports `MISSING`/`STALE`/`EXTRA` drift and returns 1 — yet Barter's manifest never names it, so `expect: "exit-0"` on `--check` would close the brief's dsh-link gap with no engine change. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dsh/sync-skills-dsh.cjs:46] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/dsh/sync-skills-dsh.cjs:317]

`sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs` follows the same shape — no flag writes, `--check` collects `STALE`/`MISSING`/`EXTRA` drift and exits non-zero — so runtime-mirror regeneration is also a manifest entry, not an engine feature. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/runtime-mirrors/sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs:70] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/runtime-mirrors/sync-runtime-mirrors.cjs:317]

The trigger index already has the exact `fresh-true` contract the engine's `verifyGenerated` expects: `generate-trigger-index.mjs --check --json` returns a `fresh` boolean and exits 1 when a document is stale or the corpus is untrusted, so regeneration plus freshness is one manifest pair. [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:33] [SOURCE: .skilled/skills/system-spec-kit/runtime/cli/retrieval/generate-trigger-index.mjs:565]

The advisor graph is the one surface the engine cannot fully express: rebuilding is `skill-advisor.cjs advisor_rebuild` (operator-gated, no freshness output), and the only checkable surface is `skill-graph-freshness.cjs`, which is report-only, exits 0 by default, and gates only under `--strict`; so a manifest can only pair an `advisor_rebuild` regenerate step with a `skill-graph-freshness.cjs --strict` exit-0 verify, never a `fresh-true` expectation. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/skill-graph-freshness.cjs:1] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/skill-graph-freshness.cjs:20]

The re-pin workflow's own invariant claims the stage runs every step on a copy, but the engine deliberately strips `regenerate` and `verifyGenerated` from a staged run, so a clean `RESULT: STAGED` report can precede a live re-pin whose regeneration fails; the two contracts disagree and the stage report carries no line saying regeneration was skipped. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/assets/doctor-overlay-repin.yaml:40] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:2914]

Regeneration steps are arbitrary argv run with `cwd` at the tree root and no allowlist, so a vendored repo's manifest is an execution surface: whoever writes `manifest.regenerate` decides what a re-pin runs, which is why a migration should copy a reviewed step list rather than accept one from an untrusted overlay folder. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1478] [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/overlay-engine.cjs:1531]

Doctor already treats the dsh surfaces as first-class mirrors, with `dsh_skills`, `dsh_prompts` and `dsh_agents` scripted against `.dsh/skills`, `.dsh/prompts` and `.dsh/agents`, so a re-pin that omits `.dsh` from its runtime folders contradicts the doctor model, not just Barter's runbook. [SOURCE: .skilled/commands/doctor/scripts/tests/doctor-runtime-mirrors-contract.test.cjs:46]

ruledOut: Assuming the engine needs a new regeneration mechanism
Assuming the advisor graph can be treated like the other generators
Trusting the repin workflow stage invariant
Looking for an engine-level post-repin hook
